This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.5 (WCAG edition). It covers **Lumen 0.1.0** (web, desktop and mobile) against **WCAG 2.2** levels A and AA, and was last reviewed on **2026-11-14**. It is published again with every major release: `node scripts/acr.mjs --check` fails when the report's version and the app's differ.

## Summary

| Level | Supports | Partially supports | Does not support | Not applicable | Of which not yet verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 22 | 5 | 0 | 4 | 13 |
| AA | 16 | 6 | 0 | 2 | 9 |

**Not yet verified:** a status that rests on an end-to-end (e2e) spec that has not run on this version. The specs are written; they run on the owner's machine before the release, and the mark goes when their run is recorded (`reports/e2e-runs.json`).

## How it was evaluated

Automated: axe-core on six surfaces in Hebrew and English, light and dark (e2e/a11y.spec.ts); reflow at 320 and 640 px and forced colours (e2e/reflow.spec.ts); spoken announcements (e2e/sr-announce.spec.ts); unit tests of the focus trap, contrast and toasts. Manual: review of each criterion against the app's code and behaviour for this version. The automated part is generated from an axe-core run (docs/acr/axe.json, scripts/acr-axe.mjs): each criterion shows the axe rules that test it, and a criterion axe finds a violation of can't be reported as supported. The end-to-end specs above have not run on this version yet (there is no CI runner; they run on the owner's Mac before the release): every status that rests on one is marked "not yet verified" until its run is recorded.

## Automated testing

**axe-core 4.11.3**, the app's components in headless Chromium, with the app's compiled CSS (offline harness), on 2026-11-14 (commit `ad415c29a3`): 159 runs on 53 surfaces × 3 setups (he/light, he/dark, en/light), 32 WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA rules, **4 rules with violations**. The "axe" column below shows, for each criterion, the rules that test it and how they came out. axe tests only part of WCAG; the rest is checked by hand, as described above.

Not tested this way (covered by the e2e suite): SearchDialog, HelpPanel.

## Exceptions and remediation plan

Every criterion not fully supported, and what will be done about it:

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content** (A, Partially supports): Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** (A, Partially supports): Give the calendar grid real rows (role=row with display: contents) and the day button inside its cell — done in #522 (W6.30); the next axe run after it lands turns this back to supports. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.1 Use of Color** (A, Partially supports): Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard** (A, Partially supports): Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.4.2 Page Titled** (A, Supports): Show the open note's name in the page title. Target: 0.2.0.
- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (A, Partially supports): Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Colour status text with the text tokens --ok/--warn (≥ 4.5:1) instead of the fill tokens — done in #522 (W6.30); re-run axe after it lands. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast** (AA, Partially supports): Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.12 Text Spacing** (AA, Partially supports): An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus** (AA, Partially supports): One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements** (AA, Partially supports): A menu or button alternative for canvas, kanban, chapter order and image resize, each with a test. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Keep the browser scan at zero on the ten surfaces; the calendar header and the usability panel are checked when the gate runs on the Mac. Target: 0.2.0.

## EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (2026-09) (VPAT 2.5 INT)

This part maps the report to clauses 9 (web), 10 (non-web documents) and 11 (non-web software) of the European standard, in the structure of the VPAT® 2.5 INT edition. Every row has a status; no row is "not evaluated".

Clause lists checked on 2026-11-15 against the criteria for apps published by the Austrian accessibility monitoring body (digitalbarrierefrei.at, 'Kriterien für Apps (ab Ende 2026)', EN 301 549 V4.1.1) and the Deque summary of V4.1.1. Clause 11.8 (authoring tools) is listed from the standard's structure; check the row numbers against the ETSI PDF before signing the report.

| 9.3.2.1 On Focus (WCAG 3.2.1) | Supports | Focusing a control never changes the context. |
| 9.3.2.2 On Input (WCAG 3.2.2) | Supports | Changing a setting applies it in place (the theme, the language); nothing navigates away or submits on input. |

| 9.3.3.7 Redundant Entry (WCAG 3.3.7) | Supports | No process asks for the same information twice; the setup wizard keeps what was entered when you go back. |

### Clause 10: Non-web documents

Lumen ships no non-web documents: its help and these reports are web pages (clause 9). Documents people write and export with Lumen are their own content; how Lumen helps make them accessible is clause 11.8.

| Row | Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Non-web documents | Not applicable | Lumen ships no non-web documents: its help and these reports are web pages (clause 9). Documents people write and export with Lumen are their own content; how Lumen helps make them accessible is clause 11.8. |

### Clause 11: Non-web software

The desktop app (Tauri) and the mobile apps (Capacitor) are the same interface in the platform's web view (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK, Android WebView), so each clause 11 row that comes from WCAG has the status of that criterion. Lumen has no closed functionality: every feature works with the platform's assistive technology. V4.1.1 does not apply WCAG 1.2.4, 2.4.1, 2.4.5, 3.1.2, 3.2.3 and 3.2.6 to non-web software.

## Accessibility contact

Hit a barrier? Open an [accessibility report](https://github.com/talstilkol/lumen-md/issues/new?template=accessibility.yml) (a form labelled **accessibility**), or choose **Report an accessibility problem** in the command palette. Accessibility reports are triaged before other bugs. See also the [accessibility statement](/editor/accessibility-statement/).
